title: Remove a broken key so the door cylinder works with its spare
instruction: Clear this lock so the spare key can be used.
fault: Correct key blade is broken flush with cylinder face while plug is turned; pins physically retain the blade until plug returns to withdrawal orientation.
justification: Common household lock failure and restoration of ordinary key operation. Importance risk remains: reviewer1675 excluded specialist lock-picking; extraction is restoration, not bypass/picking.
objects: Full-scale enclosed Schlage Classic geometry reconstruction, six pin stacks and keyway
Broken key blade and matching intact spare
Ordinary thin hooked key extractor and turning tool
Door-board mounting fixture and catch tray
skill: Return turned plug with broken key to withdrawal position; engage a key cut through narrow keyway and extract blade, then verify spare-key operation.
scoring: Provisional: fragment physically clear and captured; matching spare key turns plug through open/closed states twice; final withdrawal and tool release. No pose-triggered coupling, fragment removal or lock bypass counts.

nearest.decision: Enlarged cut-away trainer exposed driver pins; specialist lock-picking below jobs threshold and not everyday.
nearest.distinct: Enclosed actual-scale cylinder; no direct pin access; goal is extracted broken key plus spare-key function, not unauthorized bypass.

nearest.decision: Oversized cylinders in square wells, block key and fixed plug omitted actual geometry and function.
nearest.distinct: Source-scale physical key cuts, round pins and enclosed cylindrical bore, but extractor access and complete function remain unvalidated.

risks: Importance is uncertain; extraction is less broadly firsthand than ordinary unlocking.
Keyway warding/plug dimensions must be measured or sourced, not invented large clearances.
Thin extractor and pin contact stability at actual scale.
Need physical retention at turned plug and release only through real pin geometry.
